question: Both address binary MCI vs cognitively normal, but through different broad channels: resting-state EEG in P-117 (Aljalal et al. 2024; the right PDF is 1-s2.0-S1746809423008959, and the pack file is an MRI-PET fusion paper) against linguistic features from conversational transcripts in P-6 (Pourramezan Fard et al. 2024). Condition 1 fails on the channel.
metric: Accuracy, MCI vs normal, in both (matched in type). The evaluation unit differs: EEG segments in P-117, subjects in P-6.

figures.P-117: Accuracy 99.81% (11 NSGA channels, ensemble KNN) and 99.51% with all channels, 10-fold CV over 3660 segments from 61 participants (29 aMCI/32 HC). Wilson with subject n=61: (0.937, 1.000).
figures.P-6: Subject-level accuracy 85.16% (SD 5.76 over 5 subject-level folds), AUC 84.75%, 68 I-CONECT participants. Wilson with n=68: (0.748, 0.917); from the fold SD, SE = 5.76/sqrt(5) = 2.58 -> (80.1, 90.2).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure: neither paper uses the other's channel, cohort or evaluation unit.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% from internal 10-fold CV over segments of 61 participants, with no external cohort. The registry flag is false only because its Best_Metric is 'not reported'. P-6 is not excluded (85.16%).
reason: Task and metric type match, and the figures differ beyond uncertainty, but the pair fails condition 1 (EEG against speech and language) and condition 5 (P-117's 99.81% on internal segment-level CV of 61 participants with no external cohort). A performance comparison resting on P-117 cannot qualify.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method. (document: 1-s2.0-S1746809423008959)
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.
divided into 3660 segments (1740 segments from MCI cases and 1860 from HC cases)
Since the number of available subjects in the I-CONECT dataset is 68, we assess the performance of our framework using the K-fold validation technique.
the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.
